chunks: And Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abbas from Abdullah al-Kahili from Abu al-Faraj who said:

I performed tawaf with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) for five paces, then I said, 'I intend to visit a sick person.' He said, 'Preserve your place, then go and visit him, then return and complete your tawaf.'

And no one should say, 'Why did you not interpret these two narrations as referring to voluntary tawaf, and make re-performance obligatory in obligatory tawaf in all cases?' Because the ruling does not differ in that matter if half is permitted, whether the tawaf is obligatory or voluntary, in that it is permissible to build upon it. And that which indicates this is what has been narrated:

key_terms.أَشْوَاط: Paces or circuits of the tawaf
key_terms.الْبِنَاءُ: Building upon/resuming from the previous point

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on pausing and resuming tawaf during Hajj?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Musa ibn al-Qasim to demonstrate Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) practical application of resuming tawaf after a brief interruption for visiting a sick person. The text explicitly refutes the objection that this leniency might only apply to voluntary tawaf, establishing that the ruling of continuity (building upon the partial tawaf) is consistent for both obligatory and non-obligatory circumambulations. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that minor, valid interruptions do not invalidate the continuity of the ritual act.
